{{Quote|I'm just a simple man trying to make my way in the universe.|Jango Fett|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />}}
'''Jango Fett''' was a renowned [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]], and the father of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], a genetic [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of his, whom he raised as a son. A [[Human/Legends|Human]] from [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]], Fett was adopted by Mandalorian warriors following the [[Death/Legends|murder]] of his parents and the disappearance of his older sister [[Arla Fett|Arla]] in [[58 BBY/Legends|58 BBY]]. Years later, he would go on to lead them through much of the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]] as [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]]. After being imprisoned by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], Fett was responsible for destroying the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], a Mandalorian group who killed Fett's mentor and surrogate father, [[Jaster Mereel]].

Following the conclusion of that conflict, Fett became a bounty hunter, quickly establishing a reputation as being one of the best in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Later on, Fett agreed to serve as the genetic template for the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clones]] that would form the bulk of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. When [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] located Jango and Boba on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], Fett fled to join [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. Though struck down by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] in combat, Fett's legacy would live on through his son Boba, as well as his cloned brethren, who would have a profound impact on galactic history.

==Biography==
===Early life (66 BBY&mdash;58 BBY)===
{{Quote|Welcome to the Mandalorians.|Jaster Mereel|<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons" />}}
[[File:Jango_kid.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Jango Fett as a young boy on [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]]]]
Born to a family of farmers, Fett grew up alongside his older sister [[Arla Fett|Arla]] on the world of [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]],<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons" /> an agricultural [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]], known for being long associated with the Mandalorians.<ref name="Triple Zero">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> [[Fett (Elder Journeyman Protector)|Fett's father]] served as a [[Journeyman Protector/Legends|Journeyman Protector]], a civilian lawman on Concord Dawn, having taken over the role when the former Protector, [[Jaster Mereel]], was exiled and joined the Mandalorians.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 1">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 1|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 1]]</ref> At some point during his youth, Fett was inoculated against the [[Karatos Plague]], a disease native to his homeworld.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 4]]</ref>

Fett was just a young boy when the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]] began between the [[True Mandalorians]], led by [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] Jaster Mereel, and a traitorous scion of their ranks, [[Tor Vizsla]]&mdash;leader of the violent Mandalorian splinter faction, the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]. When the war [[Battle of Concord Dawn|spilled]] on to Fett's homeworld, his father granted Jaster Mereel and his men refuge at [[Fett homestead|their homestead]]. Curious about footprints he found in the field, Fett questioned his father who merely remarked that there were beggars he was feeding and told Fett to get back to his chores. The Death Watch caught up with the True Mandalorians at the homestead and Tor Vizsla captured Fett while he was fixing the family's [[Harvester/Legends|harvester]], using him in an attempt to root Mereel and his men out of hiding. Vizsla savagely beat Fett's father in front of the boy while he demanded the location of the hidden Mandalorians, even going so far as threatening to shoot him in the head right in front of his son. However, [[Jango Fett's mother|Fett's mother]] intervened, shooting one of the Death Watch in the face with a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] and in the ensuing chaos, Fett's father ordered his son to run. Fleeing into the nearby crop field, Fett was rescued by Mereel and his soldiers while his parents were murdered<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 1" /> and his sister taken by the Death Watch.<ref name="ImpCom">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>

[[File:Concorddawn.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Jaster Mereel rescues Fett from the Death Watch.]]
As the Death Watch set fire to the fields, Fett led the True Mandalorians to an irrigation tube that allowed them to escape the blaze.They took Fett with them as they fled the homestead, the Death Watch burning the crop fields they took cover in. With his family dead and his home in ruins, Fett joined the Mandalorians as they regrouped in a nearby town in order to stage an ambush on the Death Watch. Believing their enemies dead, Vizsla and his men moved into the town on a celebratory raid, only to come under fire from the Mandalorians, attacking from street alleys and high windows. Using the firefight as a distraction, Fett planted an explosive charge beneath the Death Watch's [[Death Watch tank|armored tank]], destroying it. He was attacked moments later by the Death Watch soldier responsible for the deaths of his parents and although the rogue Mandalorian slashed him with his [[Gauntlet/Legends|gauntlet's]] [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]], Fett was able to snatch up a blaster, shooting and killing his parents' murderer. Having proven himself in Mereel's eyes, after the fighting was over Fett was taken in by the ''Mand'alor'', who raised the boy as he would be his own son.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 1" /> Unbeknownst to Fett, his sister Arla also survived the battle, taken prisoner by the Death Watch and later held for years in a [[Valorum Center|mental institution]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] until [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

[[File:Jangoteenager.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Fett embraces his new identity as a Mandalorian warrior.]]
Now a Mandalorian, Jango Fett would continue to fight alongside Mereel and his forces into his teenage years and until the [[Battle of Korda Six]]. His first time as a squad commander, the mission promised to be little more than a basic extraction operation. Employed by the [[Korda Defense Force]], the Mandalorians were to recover a team of rookie security personnel pinned down under fire by a group of local hostiles, supposedly poorly armed and with no formal army. Placed in charge of the group humorously referred to as "Jango's Grunts", Fett and his team were in charge of providing cover fire and ensuring that the extraction point remained clear of danger. However, the intelligence reports turned out to be inaccurate and the claims of "minimal resistance" turned out to be a much heavier force. When Mereel's second-in-command, [[Montross (bounty hunter)|Montross]], refused to retreat and was injured in a [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]] strike, it was up to Mereel to save him. At the same time, Fett used Montross' ill-guided attack as a diversion to move on their original objective. But when he reached the site, the expected team of security personnel in need turned out to be a Death Watch ambush. While Fett fought back the Death Watch soldiers, Mereel and Montross came under attack by Vizsla himself.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 2]]</ref>

[[File:SWJFOS2.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Fett cradles his adoptive father, Jaster Mereel, as he dies.]]
It was then that Montross, through with taking Mereel's orders, abandoned the seriously injured ''Mand'alor'' and left him to die by Vizsla's hand. Though Fett rushed to the aid of the man who'd raised him like a father, he was too late to save him as Vizsla unleashed his tank's [[Laser cannon/Legends|cannons]] on the injured soldier. It was in Fett's arms that Mereel passed away. At the landing zone, Montross urged the Mandalorians to heed Mereel's final orders and pull out, claiming that both Mereel ''and'' Fett were dead. However, Fett not only returned to the landing zone at that very moment, but carried with him Jaster Mereel's body. Still Montross continued in his attempts to seize control, implying that Mereel would have wanted him to take over as the new ''Mand'alor'' and that the Mandalorians would do best with him in command. But when Fett revealed the truth of Montross' betrayal&mdash;that he'd left their beloved leader to die alone on the battlefield&mdash;the other Mandalorians denounced Montross at blaster point and proclaimed that they would follow only Fett. Montross was allowed to leave, cursing Fett as he slipped off into exile, while Jango Fett became the new ''Mand'alor'', leader of the Mandalorians.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2" />

===Leading the Mandalorians===
{{Quote|You were ''at'' Galidraan&hellip;tell me, how did one mere man kill so many of your kind?''"<br />"''With his bare hands.|[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]], speaking about Jango Fett|<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons" />}}
[[File:Jango_escape.jpg|thumb|left|Fett escapes a Death Watch ambush on Galidraan.]]
As the new ''Mand'alor'', Fett led the Mandalorians much as Jaster Mereel had done before him. Twenty-two years before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], Fett and his Mandalorians were hired to put down an insurrection on the planet [[Galidraan/Legends|Galidraan]]. When the fighting was over and the rebels defeated, Fett ordered his men to return to their camp while he met with Galidraan's [[Governor of Galidraan|governor]] to collect their payment. In addition to their pay, Fett demanded the whereabouts of Tor Vizsla whom the Governor of Galidraan was not only harboring, but funding in his attempts to rebuild the Death Watch. Vizsla revealed himself there in the governor's castle and attacked Fett with a small cadre of Death Watch soldiers, forcing Fett to flee the building through a large window. Unfortunately, Vizsla and the governor had already put a plot into motion, claiming that Mandalorians were murdering "political activists", along with women and children&mdash;with Vizsla's own forces providing the body count of innocents&mdash;and begging the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] to step in and put a stop to them.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 3">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 3|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 3]]</ref>

[[File:MandaloriansOnGalidraan-JFOS3.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Fett and the Mandalorians attacking the Jedi.]]
As the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|ships]] began to land, Fett desperately tried to warn his second-in-command, [[Myles]], and the other Mandalorians to evacuate the camp, but his helmet's [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] had been damaged in his escape from Vizsla and they only received Fett's warning when he arrived seconds before the Jedi team. Led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Komari Vosa]], the Jedi took the governor at his word and called on the Mandalorians to surrender on suspected murder charges and promised a fair treatment, with Vosa adding that should they choose fight them, the Jedi will "bring swift justice". Innocent and indignant, Fett ordered his troops to open fire, specifically on Vosa whom he called a "loudmouth".<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2" /> When their [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] were reflected back at them by the Jedi's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], Fett ordered the use of projectiles and provision of cover via [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpacks]]. Even when attacking them from above, however, Myles was [[Sai tok/Legends|cut in half]] by one of the Jedi while assisting Fett in a charge.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 3" />

[[File:GalidraanFaceoff-jfos.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Fett faces off against Myles' killer.]]
It was then that Fett would carry out the act that would make him both famous and infamous for the rest of his life and career: using no weapon beyond his own hands, feet, and armored body, Fett vengefully killed six Jedi, including the one who killed Myles.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 3" /> His efforts, although impressive, couldn't change the outcome of the battle. As a result of the Death Watch's machinations and Fett's aggressive reaction, the True Mandalorians were wiped out. Fett, the sole Mandalorian survivor of the battle, was subdued by the Jedi who were forced to deliver him into the custody of the Governor of Galidraan. Stripped of his [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|armor]], he was sold into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]].<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4" /> The Death Watch had won at last.

[[File:Jangovsvizsla.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Fett is unrelenting in his vengeance upon Vizsla.]]
Fett spent years as a slave aboard a [[Transport/Legends|spice transport]], until his chance at freedom came when [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] attacked the ship. Though his slave masters promised him freedom if he helped them fend off the attack, Fett had already broken free of his restraints and with a stolen [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], killed the slaver before fighting his way off the ship. Once free of the spice freighter, he set his sights on Galidraan, going after his lost armor and his revenge upon the governor.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4" /> Slipping by all of the governor's security, Fett infiltrated his castle, recovered his armor&mdash;restored and repainted by the governor as a trophy&mdash;and offered the governor a choice: his life or the location of the Death Watch.
Intercepting the ''[[Death Rattle]]'', Vizsla's personal [[Starship/Legends|starship]], over [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], Fett used a [[Jango Fett's starfighter|starfighter]] to cripple the ship's engines while assaulting the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], using his jetpack to fly through the [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]]. He clashed with Vizsla in a lengthy fight that spanned the halls of the dying ship and even into an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]], continuing on after crashing to the surface of Corellia. After tumbling into a river, Vizsla stabbed Fett between the armor plates on his torso with a poisoned blade, taunting him that Jaster Mereel would be disappointed. In response, Fett used the blade on his gauntlet to carve a deep wound across Vizsla's abdomen, drawing a pack of nearby [[dire-cat]]s that attacked and killed Vizsla but spared Fett due to the poison.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4" />

[[File:JangoFett-OP.png|thumb|left|170px|Fett's refurbished armor]]
In [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]], Fett somehow lost his armor in the [[Meridian sector/Legends|Meridian sector]]. While searching for it, he met a woman named [[Sheeka Tull]]. She helped him find his armor, and they began a relationship. The two spent a year together, which ended when their ship was attacked by pirates. They each entered separate escape pods and never saw each other again.<ref name="The Cestus Deception">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>

With the death of Tor Vizsla<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4" /> and the remaining few Death Watch members fleeing to the far reaches of the galaxy, the Mandalorian Civil War had come to an end but at a substantial cost to Fett. Without a war to fight or his trusted comrades to fight beside, Fett grew distant from the rest of his people and his role as ''Mand'alor'' and instead, using his combat skills, weaponry, and mercenary experience, turned to the solitary life of a bounty hunter.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> He took up residence at [[Outland Transit Station]], a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], where, with the help of a [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] female associate named [[Rozatta]], he continued his career as a bounty hunter and soldier-for-hire utilizing Jaster Mereel's former ship, now bearing the name ''[[Jaster's Legacy]]''.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref>

===The hunt for Komari Vosa===
{{Quote|Greetings, Jango Fett. I am Tyranus. I have a proposition for you: you are one of a select few chosen to participate in a ''special'' hunt, for a ''special'' prey. If you succeed, your reward will be in the amount of five ''million'' Republic credits.|A message from Darth Tyranus to Jango Fett|<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />}}
[[File:JangoRecruited-SWBH.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Darth Tyranus makes Fett a tempting offer.]]
In the year [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Fett was tracking the [[Muttani]] criminal [[Meeko Ghintee]]. Wanted by the [[Republic Correctional Authority/Legends|Republic Correctional Authority]] for a substantial list of crimes including assault, larceny, and murder, Fett found Meeko on Outland Station where he was attempting to win a [[Pit fighting|pit fight]] by utilizing a control device on his own [[borhek]]. When Fett surprised Meeko and offered him the chance to be taken in alive, Meeko fled, commanding his borhek to attack Fett. After defeating the creature, Fett pursued Meeko on a lengthy chase through Outland Station's [[Merchant Row (Outland Station)|Merchant Row]] that ended with Fett disabling [[Longshot (Tri-Mark VII Interceptor)|Meeko's ship]] and capturing the criminal. Shortly after, Fett met with friend and Outland Station's owner, Rozatta, to collect his fee. While there, "Roz"&mdash;as she was affectionately known to the bounty hunter&mdash;passed along a message she had taken for him. In it, a man calling himself [[Dooku/Legends|Tyranus]] offered Fett the chance to participate in an exclusive hunt for former Jedi turned leader of the [[Bando Gora/Legends|Bando Gora]] cult [[Komari Vosa]], with a bounty of five million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. However, he would not be alone, as Tyranus also extended an invitation to several other bounty hunters, including Montross. Although Roz would warn Fett of the danger and the Bando Gora's ominous reputation, she provided him with a lead on a [[Death stick/Legends|death stick]] [[Slythmonger/Legends|dealer]] with possible ties to the cult operating on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

[[File:FettInterrogatesGloom-SWBH.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Fett interrogating Gloom about a new type of death stick.]]
Fett pursued [[Jervis Gloom]]&mdash;the low-life dealer Roz had turned him on to&mdash;throughout [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City's]] [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|entertainment district]], and upon locating him at his warehouse, he captured and forced Gloom to reveal who he was working for and where the death sticks he sold were coming from. This information led to a [[Nerf/Legends|nerf]] [[Haugg Nerf Industries|processing plant]] in Coruscant's industrial district, owned by [[Groff Haugg]] and used as a front for shipping death sticks. Montross would prove himself a step ahead of Fett, as he'd already reached Haugg, interrogated him, and killed him by lowering him into [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] before Fett could speak with him. Haugg had lied to the disgraced Mandalorian, however, and after a brief skirmish between the two bounty hunters, Montross headed to the [[Gazzari system/Legends|Gazzari system]] while Fett searched Haugg's database and found a transmission from [[Connus Trell]], the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] from [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. Breaking into the Senator's Coruscant apartment, Fett dangled the corrupt politician from the balcony of his suite until he confessed his criminal contact was a [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] crime lord by the name of [[Sebolto]] who was manufacturing the death sticks on [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]]. Fett's investigation was cut short by the arrival of a [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|CSF]] [[Variable Altitude Assault Transport/enforcement|gunship]]; demanding that he release Trell, Fett simply replied "As you wish." before dropping the Senator to his death and engaging the police ship.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

[[File:JangoFettDesolationAlley-SWBH.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Fett fights his way through, and out of, Desolation Alley.]]
After a battle with the gunship that ended in its destruction, Fett left Coruscant and contacted Roz aboard his ship. While contemplating the best way to gain access to the Dug crime lord, Roz suggested he make a trip to the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] [[Prison/Legends|prison]] [[Oovo IV/Legends|Oovo IV]] where a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] by the name of [[Bendix Fust]] was serving time. Fust had a substantial bounty posted by Sebolto and, with Roz's advice, Fett decided that bringing Sebolto "a present", as he put it, would be a good way to gain an audience with him. Fett made for the [[Oovo asteroid belt]] with the intention of breaking the smuggler out of prison, and used [[Supply ship/Legends|Supply ship]] [[1729]] as cover to infiltrate the asteroid's shields. Fett worked his way through [[Desolation Alley]], but just as Fett reached Fust's cell, his mission was delayed when a novice bounty hunter managed to capture Fust first. The two met at gunpoint, but decided to work together to escape the locked-down prison, inciting a [[Oovo IV Uprising|riot]] in the process. Though her interference ultimately cost Fett his beloved ship, ''Jaster's Legacy'', they were able to reach the prison's hangar where six prototype [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft/Legends|''Firespray''-class starships]] were located. Stealing one of the patrol craft, Fett piloted the vessel out of the hangar before destroying the hangar and the remaining ships within. En route to Malastare with Fust secured in the cargo hold, the other bounty hunter introduced herself as [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]]. Fett was quick to chastise her reckless behavior, pointing out that she was the reason he'd lost his ship, although she considered the Firespray an improvement over the old [[Amphibious Interstellar Assault Transport/infantry|AIAT/i transport]]. Accepting the ship as his own, Fett decided to name it [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

[[File:JangoFettMalastare-SWBH.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Fett treks through Malastare's dense jungle to reach Sebolto's palace.]]
Later, Fett formed a partnership with Wesell and they mutually agreed to split the bounty when they delivered Fust to Sebolto. Heading to Malastare, Sebolto's homeworld, Fett managed to sneak inside the crime lord's palace with the help of Wesell. The [[Clawdite/Legends|Clawdite]] delivered Fust to Sebolto while Fett went in the back way, trekking his way through the dense jungle outside of Sebolto's palace. Wesell managed to get away from Sebolto and head back down the compound, where she helped Fett call a [[Skiff/Legends|skiff]] to cross a chasm separating the compound from the jungle. They then went back up the compound to Sebolto's palace with the pair of them killing anyone who got in their way. When they confronted Sebolto he frantically tried to escape, but fell into the factory's chemical mixing vat, boiling him to death. Fett then fought hordes of Bando Gora as he made his way deeper into Sebolto's death stick factory and later fought Montross as well. Reaching Sebolto's transport ship, Fett discovered [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] markings, which led Fett straight to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Two [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] and [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla Besadii the Elder]], controlled the desert planet, and one of them had connections to the Bando Gora.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

In order to gain an audience with Jabba, Fett fought a gang of outlaws led by [[Longo Two-Guns]], who had a price on his head that was posted by the Hutt. When Fett came to Jabba to collect his reward, he asked the slimy crime lord about the Bando Gora. However, it turned out that Jabba actually had nothing to do with Vosa or the crime syndicate. Instead, he informed Fett that it was Gardulla, not him, that was allied with the cult. In the meantime, Wesell managed to sneak inside Gardulla's palace but was captured, leaving Fett to fight his way inside by himself. But when he got there, Fett wanted to leave her in her cell for protection, which Wesell mistook for leaving her out of a fair 50-50 share of Vosa's bounty. She called for the guards, who then knocked Fett out and stripped him of his weapons, and then brought him to Gardulla to decide his fate. The Hutt decided to simply kill Fett by feeding the famed bounty hunter to her pet [[Krayt dragon/Legends|Krayt dragon]]. As Fett was brought to its pen, he managed to kill the guards that were at his side holding him down. Retrieving his weapons, Fett fought his way through the palace. In the end, Gardulla ended up as nearly being lunch for her own beast, but not before Fett had discovered the information he was searching for&mdash;Gardulla´s relation with the Bando Gora and their activities with the Tatooine´s Death Stick Trade. Unbeknownst to Jango, however, Gardulla survived this encounter because Fett killed her Krayt Dragon before it could completely digest her, allowing her to crawl out of its corpse.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

[[File:Jango-SWCTP.png|thumb|left|180px|Jango Fett, Mandalorian bounty hunter]]
Leaving Wesell in her cell because of her apparent betrayal, Fett set off to return to Outland Station. Unbeknownst to Fett, however, Rozatta was at the very moment under attack by Montross. It would seem the other bounty hunter had barely made a move on the bounty, instead tracking Fett through a beacon planted on his ship. Roz, despite Fett's personal motto "trust no-one", was one of the few people who cared about Fett. Revealing the location as the moon of [[Bogden/Legends|Bogden]], [[Kohlma]] her last wish was that he would find something to actually care and live for besides money. She believed that despite his dangerous line of work, he was a good and honorable man and deserved more out of life.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

Fett traveled to the Bogden system, fighting all manner of Bando Gora along the way. Having one last duel with Montross, he denied his old foe an honorable "warrior's" death, instead allowing the Bando Gora to proudly finish Montross off. Moving deeper into Vosa's lair, Fett was ambushed, knocked unconscious, and stripped of his weaponry.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

Having captured Fett, the Bando Gora prepared to turn him into a mindless slave. It was here that Fett acquired many of his facial scars. Vosa herself came to demand of him the name of his employer, but Zam Wesell freed Fett before being injured by the insane [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]]. After a long duel with Vosa, Jango Fett emerged victorious. As he prepared to finish her off, Vosa asked if he would choose to leave her dead or alive. Jango, looking at the ruined female nearing her death, lowered his weapons. Vosa murmured "He&hellip; is here." before being [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Choke|choked]] with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to her last breath.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

[[File:Vosajango.jpg|thumb|200px|Jango Fett is captured by [[Komari Vosa]].]]
To Fett's surprise, Tyranus was indeed there, and he was impressed. The bounty was a test to determine if the rumors of Fett's skills against Jedi were true.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> If so, his clones trained under his supervision would be very effective once [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], the order to eliminate all Jedi, was issued. While Fett had personally killed many Jedi on Galidraan, Tyranus considered his former apprentice a more challenging test. In addition to the bounty on Vosa, Tyranus offered Fett a tempting sum of money for an unusual task: Fett was to be a template for an army of [[Cloning/Legends|clones]]. Fett agreed, and soon millions of clones were created in his likeness at the cloning facility on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. Fett, however, remembered Rozatta's final wish and asked for one clone produced without genetic tampering, an apprentice and son that would become Jaster's legacy and revive the Mandalorians.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

Jango Fett left Kohlma and said his goodbyes to Zam Wesell (who, thanks to trauma received on Kohlma, had seemingly forgotten what Fett looked like beneath his helmet when they next encountered each other, some five years later).<ref name="Star Wars: Jango Fett">[[Star Wars: Jango Fett (one-shot)|''Star Wars: Jango Fett'']]</ref> After parting ways, he returned to Dooku's [[Dooku's castle (Kohlma)|estate]] to finalize his deal with the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]. His wish for an heir was granted and soon after the project was underway on Kamino, he was awarded the first clone whom he would name [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. Despite his later claims to the contrary, Fett was indeed aware that Tyranus was also the former Jedi Master Dooku, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] leader, having already met Dooku at the Battle of Galidraan.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons" />

===The Grand Army===
{{Quote|Apart from his pay, which is considerable, Fett demanded only one thing: an unaltered clone for himself. Curious, isn't it?|Lama Su to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], referring to Fett's request for Boba Fett|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />}}
[[File:Jango_Fett_and_Kal_Skirata.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Jango Fett and [[Kal Skirata]] oversee clone trooper training]]
Jango Fett's most famous contribution to the creation of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] was the donation of his genes used to produce the army's [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] at Kamino's [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]] facility. However, Fett would be central in many facets of the army's early development, including assisting in the design of the armor worn by the clones, evident in the loose similarities between their armor and Fett's own Mandalorian [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|shock trooper armor]], including the distinctive T-visor of their helmets.<ref name=" Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary" /> He would also become a military consultant and helped to create the [[flash training]] regimen used to instruct all of the young clones, including in it the traditional Mandalorian song ''[[Vode An]]'' as a useful tool to help instill within them with a sense of purpose, modifying it slightly in order to give it meaning for soldiers serving the Republic.<ref name="Triple Zero" /><ref name="O66" /> Fett was also responsible for recruiting the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'', a one-hundred man group&mdash;seventy-five of which were Mandalorians&mdash;with assorted skills and professions, hired to train the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] that would make up the army's special forces.<ref name="Republic Commando: Hard Contact">''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]''</ref> Fett would personally oversee the training of the one-hundred [[Alpha-class Advanced Recon Commando]]s, considered the most skilled and elite soldiers in the Grand Army.<ref name="Triple Zero" /><ref name="Republic 50">[[Republic 50|''Republic'' 50]]</ref>

Eight years prior to the Battle of Geonosis, Fett met with Mandalorian ''Cuy'val Dar'' training [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] [[Kal Skirata]] in Tipoca's cloning facility. There, he spoke with the man concerning the solitude that came with being ''Cuy'val Dar''&mdash;"Those Who No Longer Exist". He would also ask Skirata to join him in evaluating a group of clones considered to be under par by Kamino [[Chief Scientist/Legends|Chief Scientist]] [[Ko Sai/Legends|Ko Sai's]] standards. However, when they arrived in the office of [[Orun Wa]], the "defective" clones turned out to be six young clone children. Deemed too independent and uncontrollable, they were labeled [[Null-class Advanced Recon Commando|"Null-class"]] and were to be exterminated as failures until Skirata stepped in on their behalf. Fett recommended they be used as intelligence units and placed the boys under Skirata's care. That evening, Fett went to see how Skirata was coping with the boys, arriving at his room with his son Boba asleep in his arms. When Skirata asked why Boba looked like the other clones, Fett explained that Boba was his genetic clone as well, but was also his son, and worth more to him than all the credits he'd been paid.<ref name="Triple Zero" />

As the army grew in secret over the years leading up to the Battle of Geonosis, ''Cuy'val Dar'' sergeant [[Dred Priest]] was found to be operating brutal [[Battle Circle]]s in the lower levels of Tipoca, forcing the clone commandos he trained to fight one another until one couldn't fight back. After the injured began to pile up in the care of fellow ''Cuy'val Dar'' sergeant and doctor, [[Mij Gilamar]], Fett was notified and quickly put an end to the illicit fights after savagely beating Priest.<ref name="ImpCom" /> Fett was also responsible for smuggling the clone deserter ARC trooper Alpha-02&mdash;"[[Spar]]"&mdash;off Kamino in the cargo hold of ''Slave I'' to repay a favor owed to Gilamar.<ref name="O66" />

===Further exploits (32 BBY&ndash;22 BBY)===
{{Quote|There's a reason I'm the most feared bounty hunter in the galaxy&hellip;let me show him why.|Jango Fett, as he engages Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Full of Surprises">''[[Full of Surprises]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dreddon_death.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The death of Dreddon The Hutt]]
Five years before the Clone Wars, Jango Fett was hired by the Hutt crime lord, Dreddon, to assassinate Black Sun's Vigo, Antonin. Fett successfully infiltrated the man's fortress and after killing some of the guards, Jango confronted Antonin in his chambers. After exchanging some banter, Fett shot Antonin dead while he drank his alderaanian wine, to no fanfare. When returning to the Hutt's palace however, he was instead greeted by Dreddon's mangled corpse. The crime lord's killer soon revealed herself to be Zam Wesell. After a brief stand off, Fett accidentally sliped that Dreddon had hired him to kill Antonin, who in turn had hired Wesell to kill Dreddon. With no real reason to fight anymore since both their employers had been killed, both bounty hunters left on mildy hostile terms. Since he wasn't able to get his pay, Jango was forced to find a different assignment, although it hurt him to have to leave his Boba alone so soon after returning to Kamino. A different bounty came in the form of [[Ashaar Khorda]], who wanted to employ Fett in order to retrieve the statue known as the [[Infant of Shaa]].<ref name="Star Wars: Jango Fett" /> Fett was hired through Khorda's aide and intermediary, a Dug named Fernooda, who briefed him on the statue but refused to elaborate on the client behind the bounty, to Fett's annoyance. But he was persuaded to take the job in light of the last one's failure, as well as the arranged payment being higher in return for his client's anonymity. On landing at his destination, Jango briefly checked in with his housekeeping droid, MU-12, enquiring about Boba's status, and bringing up issues that had been plaguing his jetpack. The droid lamented being unable to finish working on it thanks to Fett's hasty departure, but assured him he should experience no problems with it; to Fett's skepticism. After a brief struggle through the native ruins thanks in part to his malfunctioning jetpack, Fett succeeded in attaining the statue by killing a [[Unidentified Seylott|Seylott]] native, but was confronted afterward by Zam, who had also been hired to retrieve the statue. While she gloated on successfully wresting it from Fett, she was seized from behind by one of the planet's local predators, and Jango used the distraction to make off with the statue. However, Zam called after him for help, and despite his misgivings, Fett's conscience won him over, and he went back to save Wesell. He fended off the creature with blaster fire until it released Zam, and the two set off explosives before dropping off the ledge they were on to distance themselves from the explosion. After recovering from the fall, Wesell admitted defeat and allowed Jango to take the statue in gratitude for saving her. Fett returned to his employer and handed the artifact over, but threatened to kill them if he ever saw them again for leaving crucial information out of his briefing. Collecting his payment, Jango returned to Kamino and a joyous Boba, assuring his son that he planned to stay home for a prolonged period this time. Not long afterward, however, Zam showed up on Kamino while the Fetts were playing ball- during which she met Boba for the first time- and informed Fett that the Infant of Shaa was in actuality a weapon powerful enough to destroy a planet. Khorda hoped to use the Infant's power to destroy Coruscant, and Zam intended intended to re-acquire the statue from him to save the galactic capital. The mission's lack of pay left Fett ambivalent over joining Wesell, but she finally convinced him after appealing to his love for Boba and the fact that there were thousands of children on Coruscant. The last-minute effort by Fett and Wesell [[Skirmish at Coruscant's power core|saved]] the Infant from unleashing its power within Coruscant's power core, though Jedi Master [[Yarael Poof/Legends|Yarael Poof]] sacrificed himself to contain the fracturing statue. Fett and Wesell then returned the statue to [[Seylott/Legends|Seylott]], where it was originally created, for safekeeping.<ref name="Star Wars: Zam Wesell">''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]''</ref>

[[File:Poof_death.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Fett with a dead [[Yarael Poof/Legends|Yarael Poof]]]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Jango took his son Boba to a cave on an [[Unidentified planet (balyeg)|unidentified planet]] for "flying practice". The cave was inhabited by a predator known as the [[balyeg]], and Jango sprayed his son with the scent of the [[pardlam]], the balyeg's main food source. He then told Boba to fetch a tooth from the mouth of the balyeg. A short while later, Boba returned with the tooth and asked his father why he made him do this. Jango told his son it was because there would come moments where he wouldn't have time to be scared. He had faced the most terrifying thing in the galaxy, and Boba would know that the most fearful thing he would ever face would be behind him.<ref name="Blood Ties: A Tale of Jango & Boba Fett">''[[Star Wars: Blood Ties]]''</ref>

One of Tyranus's missions, had Fett track down and eliminate a [[Connor Freeman's father|helmeted man]] on [[Atzerri/Legends|Atzerri]] that posed a threat to his plans for the clone army. After taking care of the planet's traffic control, Fett had his son Boba shoot the man. Jango then went down to question the man, who was revealed to be clone trooper deserter. Fett then shot the clone. However, he found out that he had a [[Connor Freeman's mother|wife]] and a [[Connor Freeman|son named Connor]]. He then left them alone since they were ignorant of the helmeted man's origins. However, Fett then set up an inheritance fund for Connor as compensation for killing the boy's father, under the guise that he was the boy's father.<ref name="Blood Ties: A Tale of Jango & Boba Fett" />

[[File:BobaJango-CVD.png|thumb|left|150px|Fett with his son, Boba Fett]]
{{Talesstart}}
In [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] Tyranus employed Fett to kill the leader of a resistance force determined to free Kuat's population from its servitude. Boba accompanied his father to [[Kuat City]], where Fett used the boy as bait to lure his [[Larbo|bounty]] into the open. While Fett assassinated the camp members, a young Boba threw a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] and fled into the tents. Once Fett's bounty located the boy, the colonist was horrified to learn the young boy was the son of the man sent to kill him. Fett, having finished assassinating the remaining members of the camp, tracked down Boba and demanded that Larbo release his son, slashing his way through the tent's canopy. Disgusted, Larbo asked what kind of man would use his own son as bait, though Boba replied, "Only a son can know his father's heart". After Fett killed Larbo, Boba escaped with his father aboard ''Slave I'' and informed the Count of their successful mission.<ref name="The Way of the Warrior">{{Tales|18|The Way of the Warrior (comic story)}}</ref>
{{Talesend}}

Months later, Tyranus ordered Fett to capture [[Groodo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Rodd]] of [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]], and [[Droid/Legends|droid]] engineer [[Hurlo Holowan]]. The three criminals had attempted to bring ruin to the Fondor system by blowing up Fondor's shipyards. In keeping with Mandalorian tradition, Fett allowed his then nine-year-old son Boba&mdash;old enough to begin training according to Mandalorian culture&mdash;to join him on this assignment. However, Fett learned that [[Cradossk/Legends|Cradossk]] and [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]&mdash;two other bounty hunters hired by [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]]&mdash;were stalking the same target.<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 4: Jango Fett vs. the Razor Eaters ">''[[Star Wars Adventures 4: Jango Fett vs. the Razor Eaters]]''</ref>

Fett succeeded in capturing Rodd, but with one setback&mdash;while his guard was down, Boba was temporarily captured by Bossk and brought before Cradossk.<ref name=" Star Wars Adventures 4: Jango Fett vs. the Razor Eaters" /> After liberating Boba from the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]], Fett was reluctant to continue his assignment until Boba was out of harm's way. He subcontracted Zam Wesell to go after Hurlo Holowan while Fett brought Boba back to the safety of Kamino. Fett also contacted Tyranus to find out who hired Cradossk and have him taken off the job.<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 5: The Shape-Shifter Strikes ">''[[Star Wars Adventures 5: The Shape-Shifter Strikes]]''</ref>

After the capture of Holowan, Fett went to [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]] to capture Groodo the Hutt. Groodo had been hiding at the well-defended castle of his brother [[Rigorra]], the planetary warlord. On Balmorra, Fett ran into [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]], who had been hunting Rigorra herself for personal reasons. The two hunters successfully infiltrated Rigorra's palace together but were captured along with two other bounty hunters&mdash;Bossk and [[Skorr/Legends|Skorr]]&mdash;who were also hunting Groodo. Fett and Sing managed to escape from Rigorra's clutches and capture their targets. Fett then delivered Rodd, Holowan and Groodo to Count Dooku on Geonosis, and departed. This would be one of the final missions Fett undertook in his life.<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 6: The Warlords of Balmorra">''[[Star Wars Adventures 6: The Warlords of Balmorra]]''</ref>

On contract for the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], Fett was hired to hunt down the Toydarian known as [[Reti]], due to his predations on Trade Federation assets on [[Maramere]]. Fett pursued Reti to [[Nod Kartha]] before he finally caught up with him in a flurry of laser cannon blasts from ''Slave I''. The Toydarian fired his hyperdrive to escape Fett but the ultimate outcome of the hunt is unknown, though Fett certainly survived.<ref name="Jedi Starfighter">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter]]''</ref>

===On the eve of war (22 BBY)===
{{Quote|Do you like your army?''"<br />"''I look forward to seeing them in action.''"<br />"''They'll do their job well. I'll guarantee that.|Jango Fett and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />}}
[[File:JangoFlying-AotC.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Jango Fett fires at [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].]]
Ten years after the Grand Army had begun on Kamino, the formation of the clone army had progressed to the point where two-hundred thousand units were ready, with approximately a million more ready shortly. Fett was hired by Trade Federation [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] to assassinate [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. Teaming with Zam Wesell again, Fett targeted the Senator on Coruscant, but the [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|plot to assassinate her]] failed and Fett was forced to kill Wesell, in order to keep his identity secret. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] traced the toxic [[Mk I Saberdart/Legends|saberdart]] Fett used to kill Wesell to Kamino and learned of the clone army of which the Jedi were previously unaware. Fett and Kenobi met in Fett's Tipoca City quarters on civil terms, with Fett going so far as to claim it was "always a pleasure to meet a Jedi" in spite of his adversarial past with the Order. However, he knew Kenobi's presence would mean trouble and had Boba quickly pack his belongings aboard ''Slave I''. When Kenobi later tried to apprehend Fett for further questioning, they clashed in a [[Mission to Kamino (Separatist Crisis)/Legends|titanic battle]] on ''Slave I''{{'s}} landing platform, culminating in Fett escaping with Boba aboard ''Slave I''.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /><ref name=" The New Essential Chronology" /><ref name="Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive">''[[Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive]]''</ref>

[[File:Jango_version_Slave_1.png|thumb|right|220px|Fett piloting ''Slave I'' amidst the Geonosis asteroid belt]]
Unfortunately for him, Fett was unaware of a [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing device]] Kenobi had attached to the ship's outer hull that enabled him to track the bounty hunter and his son to [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]]. When Fett discovered Kenobi's presence, a [[Dogfight over Geonosis/Legends|dogfight over Geonosis]] ensued, and although Fett had the upper hand for much of the skirmish, Kenobi was able to outsmart Fett by creating the illusion [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|his ship]] had been destroyed while in fact he lay in wait on one of the asteroids in Geonosis' rings. Fett was able to land on the planet's surface and meet up with Dooku and the other members of the fledgling [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Kenobi would be found alive shortly afterward, captured after spying on Dooku and the other Separatist leaders, and sentenced to death in the arena for espionage. When Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and Padmé Amidala attempted to rescue Kenobi, only to stumble into the complex labyrinth of the [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|Geonosis droid foundries]], Fett would lead a team of [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] in capturing Skywalker. Fett and his son Boba were special guests of the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]] and watched the execution from a private box overlooking the [[Petranaki arena]] with the Geonosian leader, Count Dooku, and Nute Gunray.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

The execution did not go as planned, as all three prisoners managed to free themselves from their chains and evade the three beasts that had been let loose upon them. At one point, Gunray became so furious that he ordered Fett to deal with Amidala personally, but Dooku urged the Viceroy to be patient and that she would die. However, Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] quietly entered the box and held Fett at bay, holding the blade of his lightsaber at the bounty hunter's throat. All throughout the arena's assembled crowd, lightsabers came to life as the nearly [[Jedi assault team/Legends|two-hundred Jedi]] who had infiltrated the arena revealed themselves. When several [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|super battle droids]] arrived at the box, drawing Windu's attention from Fett, he took the opportunity to strike with his wrist-mounted [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrower]], unleashing a stream of flames at Windu, who leapt from the box and into the arena, throwing off his burning [[Jedi apparel/Legends|cloak]] after landing unharmed. A massive [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|battle]] broke out between the Jedi and the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] that poured into the arena, although Fett would remain at Dooku's side; when Jedi Council member [[Coleman Trebor/Legends|Coleman Trebor]] attempted to assault the skybox and confront Dooku, Fett unloaded several blaster bolts into the Jedi Master, killing him and knocking him off the balcony.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

Fett used his jetpack to fly down to the arena floor, where he confronted Windu, who had dropped his lightsaber. However, Windu retrieved it with a simple [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force Pull]]. A [[Reek/Legends|reek]], one of the creatures that had been let loose to execute the prisoners and was still loose, suddenly disrupted their battle, trampling Fett in the process. Fett killed it with a swift blast to the head, but his jetpack was damaged with the reek's attack. As Windu rushed in, Fett's attempts to blast him proved futile, leading him to attempt to gain space by jetting away. The jetpack upon which he relied failed to fire due to damage sustained from his earlier encounter with the reek, leaving him vulnerable to Windu's [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitating strike]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

[[File:Jangodied.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Jango Fett is beheaded by Mace Windu.]]

===Legacy===
{{Quote|The Fett name puts the very fear of ''haran'' up the ''aruetiise''.|Fenn Shysa, on Jango Fett's infamous prowess|<ref name="O66" />}}
After his death, Jango Fett's clones told themselves a different story of his death. They believed that he was unaware of Count Dooku's [[Treason/Legends|treason]] and was unwilling to malign his honor by going back on his word, and killed twelve Jedi Masters before being killed himself. Although the real details of Fett's death eventually became clear, the clones nonetheless continued to faithfully serve under their Jedi officers, including Mace Windu. Unfortunately for Fett, he never lived to see his clones participate in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a conflict which tore the galaxy apart and cleared the way for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Nor would he ever see his son, Boba, continue his bounty hunting legacy, using his father's weapons and ship, as well as the suit of Mandalorian armor once worn by Jaster Mereel.<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> Boba tried to avenge his father by sabotaging the Jedi cruiser [[Endurance/Legends|''Endurance'']] in order to kill Windu, though the plan failed.<ref name="Death Trap">{{TCW|Death Trap}}</ref><ref name="Lethal Trackdown">{{TCW|Lethal Trackdown}}</ref>

[[File:Bloodties2.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] followed in the footsteps of his slain father in becoming a bounty hunter.]]
Jango Fett was buried on Geonosis by Boba with the simple initials J.F. on a headstone.<ref name="Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive" /> In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] Boba, along with his granddaughter [[Mirta Gev]], retrieved Fett's remains from Geonosis so that they could be buried on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] next to Boba's daughter, [[Ailyn Vel]].<ref name="Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref>

In honor of the legendary bounty hunter, a gladiatorial pit that became known as the [[Jango Fett Arena]] was built in the city of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy" /> [[Fenn Shysa]] respected Fett and his skill so greatly that he firmly believed a descendant, relative, or clone of Fett would be the best choice to lead the Mandalorians. He hoped to utilize Fett's fierce reputation as a [[Jedi hunter/Legends|Jedi killer]] as a symbol of strength for Mandalore.<ref name="O66" /> On [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], however, he was not held in high regard by the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction, with their Prime Minister [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] dismissing him as a mere bounty hunter who had obtained Mandalorian armor via unknown means.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> Only after Spar brought the warrior traditions of the Mandalorian culture back to the forefront of their society as "Mandalore the Resurrector" and the New Mandalorians declined in influence, was Fett's memory rehabilitated in the minds of mainstream Mandalorian society&mdash;though Spar, himself, considered Fett a disgrace for allowing the Kaminoans to clone a slave army from his genes.<ref name="O66" />

After his death, Jango Fett's legacy was carried on not only by Boba Fett, but also by the millions of clone troopers based on his template. After the Clone Wars, Fett's clones were continuously used as soldiers of the Republic's successor state, the Galactic Empire. At least until the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Fett clones were maintained within the ranks of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], despite gradually becoming a small minority in an army increasingly diversified between enlisted troopers and clones based on different templates.<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I want the first clone for myself, unmodified.''"<br />"''Might I inquire as to why?''"<br />"''You might.|Jango Fett and Count Dooku|<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />}}
[[File:JangoFett-NEC.jpg|thumb|A portrait of Jango Fett]]
Jango Fett was thorough, instinctive, and ruthless when it came to bounty hunting, but he was known to have a soft side for the few people he cared about in life. He was often motivated by money, and as such his loyalty was to the highest bidder. He became so efficient in bounty hunting that even planetary governments were known to hire him.<ref name="Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

Fett kept himself in top condition, maintaining the habit of training often with his equipment.<ref name=" Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary" /> He was also very intelligent, having prudent tactical skills, and was fluent in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]],<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" /> and [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']].<ref name="Triple Zero" /> He was also able to read [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]], [[Mandalorian (writing system)/Legends|''Mandalorian'']]<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> and used [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic]] on his [[Mando'a/Legends|''buy'ce's'']] HUD. Nonetheless, he would always prefer a subtle approach to his hunting, a trait that he would pass on to his son.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref>

Fett kept a cool demeanor when calculating his every move, always playing to win or survive. He knew best when to make use of evasion, which enabled him to outlast his enemies.<ref name=" Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary " /> In fact, it was only when his evasion skills did fail him, at the Battle of Geonosis, that he was defeated and killed.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

[[File:Jango_OS_TPB.png|thumb|left|150px|Jango Fett takes aim while employing his jetpack.]]
Fett also worked out his own [[Jango Fett's code|moral code]] that he deemed honorable by his standards. He would live much of his life as a bounty hunter following these guidelines. Later, he would raise his son Boba by these codes, which shaped what type of missions Boba would undertake in his own lifetime.<ref name="Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive" /> [[Hondo Ohnaka/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka]] would later invoke Jango's preference for doing the honorable thing to convince his son Boba to tell Plo Koon where Aurra Sing and Bossk were keeping their hostages so they could be rescued.<ref name="Lethal Trackdown" />

Fett preferred to work alone; however, he would occasionally partner with Zam Wesell when working together was in their best interest.<ref name="Star Wars: Jango Fett" /><ref name="Star Wars: Zam Wesell" /> He also worked with his associate Rozatta early in his career as a bounty hunter.<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" /> However, other than Wesell and Roz, Fett was a loner who usually kept to himself, most likely because of Montross' betrayal, which had cost Jaster Mereel his life.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons" /> Through bounty hunting, Fett had garnered at least 5,527,200 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

Consistent with his preference for working alone, Fett also chose to live alone. He never married or formed long-term relationships; and it seemed that he would never have any offspring. However, the Kamino cloning enterprise gave him an unexpected opportunity to raise a son who was an exact genetic replica of himself&mdash;unlike the usual kind of offspring, whose genes are a random mixture of genes from mother and father. In addition to his pay, he requested an unaltered clone for himself. By specifying that this particular clone be genetically unaltered and grow at the normal, non accelerated rate, Fett could reasonably expect that Boba Fett would learn all the skills and values he wanted to teach him.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" />

In contrast to his relationship with Boba, Fett had no personal feelings toward the other clones save perhaps the ARC Troopers he personally trained. He considered the cloning contract no different than any other, and despite Kal Skirata's apprehension about working with the Jedi on the army's creation, Fett displayed his neutrality by simply pointing out that it was just business.

===Relationships===
====[[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]====
[[File:JangoBobaFett_JFOS.png|thumb|right|200px|Jango with his "son," Boba.]]
When serving as the clone template for the Kaminoans, Jango asked for an unaltered clone in addition to his fee whom he named Boba and raised as his son. Jango also stated that he is an apprentice and is also "Jaster's Legacy", but he firmly believed that Boba was worth far more than the five million credits he was rewarded for defeating Vosa. During Boba's upbringing, he taught him how to use a blaster.

====[[Jaster Mereel]]====
Mereel was Jango's surrogate father when he was a young Mandalorian. Jango had huge amounts of respect for him and firmly believed that he would always do what was right for the Mandalorians. Jango was deeply saddened when Mereel died and took on his role as the leader of the Mandalorians.

====[[Sheeka Tull]]====
Sheeka Tull was Jango's girlfriend when he was twenty-five years old and courted for a year before their ship was boarded by pirates. After they went into separate escape pods, they never saw each other again.

====[[Rozatta]]====
Rozatta was Jango's assistant during his early career as a bounty hunter, finding bounties and looking out for him as long as she got her finder's fee. Roz and Jango often joked with each other, Roz being one of the only people he could trust. He was very upset when Montross blew up Outland Station, killing her, and when Jango got the job for the clone army he requested an unaltered clone to raise as a son, something Roz wanted him to live for.

====[[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]]====
Zam and Jango had a friendly professional relationship but were often arguing about strategies due to Jango feeling that she was reckless and should learn how to be subtle. The two had great respect for each other and Zam was an important person in young Boba's life before he was forced to kill her. She often teased Jango.

====[[Kal Skirata]]====
Kal Skirata knew Jango during the days when they were both active Mandalorians. They had an up and down relationship: while Skirata was a very aggressive Mandalorian traditionalist, Jango was more cunning and preferred subtle approaches, but they both cared greatly for the troops they served with. Jango recruited Kal for the [[Cuy'val Dar]] and asked him to assist with the [[Null-class Advanced Recon Commando|"Null" class]] [[Advanced Recon Commando|ARC Troopers]] who were going to to be terminated for being a failed experiment. Kal intervened by telling a young Ordo not to kill Orun Wa while Jango convinced her of their strategic value.

====[[Montross (bounty hunter)|Montross]]====
Montross was a Mandalorian warrior like Jango, but he hated Jango, as well as Jaster for treating him like he was his son. He betrayed Jaster by letting Tor Vizsla kill him. For this, Jango and the other Mandalorians banished him, with Jango receiving the role Jaster had, which Montross had so desperately sought. Jango encountered Montross again after receiving a transmission telling him he found Rozatta and was intending to kill her. Jango later found Montross while on his way to find Komari Vosa, and the two engaged in a fight, resulting in Montross being eaten alive by the [[Bando Gora/Legends|Bando Gora]].

====[[Silas (Mandalorian)|Silas]]====
[[File:Jango_and_Silas.jpg|thumb|[[Jango Fett|Jango]] and [[Silas (Mandalorian)|Silas]], brothers in arms.]]
Silas was an active member of the [[True Mandalorians]], he entered the faction some time after the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] supposed ''demise'' on Concord Dawn, he and [[Jango Fett|Jango]] became good friends and occasionaly worked together during missions, he was with Jango when they witnesed Jaster Mereel violent death, and prevented Jango from getting gunned down, later supporting him in his rise to the mandalore position. It is unknown how, but Silas was still alive years later after the True Mandalorians [[Battle of Galidraan|eradication]] and was aware of said event. At some point Silas was captured and tortured by the Sith Lord [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] in order to get information about Jango Fett, Silas refused, but the count was able to get the information by injecting him a powerful [[truth serum]], he later ordered the [[Interrogation droid|torture droids]] to stop Silas' heart and kill him.

==Equipment==
===Weapons and armor===
{{Quote|I'm intimately familiar with that fast draw of yours, Jango.|Zam Wesell|<ref name="Star Wars: Jango Fett" />}}
[[File:JangoFettChestArmor-FF60.png|thumb|left|200px|Fett's chest armor]]
Fett wore [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] in the "shocktrooper" style common during his time, although instead of the more traditional [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] plating, he utilized the less resilient and less expensive [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]]<ref>{{fact}} Citation needed</ref> alloy for his armor. Fett was armed with custom [[WESTAR-34 blaster pistol/Legends|WESTAR-34 blaster pistols]],<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech]] [[Dur-24 wrist laser/Legends|Dur-24 wrist laser]],<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" /> [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] [[ZX miniature flame projector/Legends|ZX miniature flame projector]] (left gauntlet), and an integrated [[Velocity-7 dart shooter]] with [[Mk I Saberdart/Legends|Kamino saberdarts]] on his right arm, among other kinds.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> Fett's left gauntlet also had a [[Kelvarek Consolidated Arms/Legends|Kelvarek Consolidated Arms]] [[MM9 mini concussion rocket launcher/Legends|MM9 mini concussion rocket]], which utilized computer target tracking.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons" /> Fett used [[Type-12A Anti-Personnel Rocket|Type-12A anti-personnel rockets]], [[Type-12B Hollow-Tip Rocket|Type-12B capsules]], and [[1126 rocket]]s.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> He also carried a [[field security overloader]], sonic beam weapon, wristband retractable blades, wrist mounted grappling hook, boot spikes, and electromagnetic devices in his gloves, enabling him to attract his guns from a short distance.<ref name="Star Wars: Jango Fett" /><ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

[[File:Jango_Fett_helmet_OS.png|thumb|right|200px|Fett's helmet]]
He had two jetpacks, one of which was a [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn]] [[JT-12 jetpack/Legends|JT-12 jetpack]]; the jetpack was personally manufactured for Jango Fett by Merr-Sonn Munitions prior to the Clone Wars. The other was a [[Z-6 jetpack/Legends|Z-6 jetpack]] manufactured by [[Mitrinomon Transports/Legends|Mitrinomon Transports]]. The JT-12 was a compact jetpack featuring a warhead missile launcher. This model was similar to the more heavily-armored Mitrinomon Z-6 jetpack. The Mitrinomon Z-6 was a more common model of jetpack used by the Mandalorians. Many Mandalorians used this type of jetpack, including Jango Fett and Boba Fett. The jetpack included a targeting computer, flight gyros, and a missile/grapple launcher. Both models were favored by the elder Fett.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> His Mandalorian helmet featured a targeting range-finder that fed him constant data, allowing him to compensate for size, speed and atmospheric conditions. The helmet had a targeting array that gave him 360-degree field of view. Built-in infrared scanners, as well as sound and motion sensors, enabled Jango to lock on to any prey from a distance and plan his attack.

[[File:Jango_Fett_blasters.png|thumb|left|200px|Fett's dual WESTAR-34 blasters]]
Oddly enough, both Jango and Boba were thwarted by their jetpacks: while fighting Obi-Wan Kenobi on Kamino, Fett's jetpack detached itself and flew out of control, exploding against a column. Also during Fett's final battle, it was the malfunction of his jetpack that ultimately resulted in his death.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> Likewise, while battling Luke Skywalker over the Pit of Carkoon, Boba's jetpack was accidentally activated by Han Solo, launching him into the side of Jabba's sail barge and into the [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlacc]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

===Vehicles===
[[File:Firespray_SotG.png|thumb|right|150px|''Slave I'']]
After the death of his mentor, Jaster Mereel, Fett inherited Mereel's personal ship. Renaming it ''[[Jaster's Legacy]]'', he used it in many of his bounty hunting contracts. During the hunt for Komari Vosa, which led to [[Oovo IV/Legends|Oovo IV]], the ship was destroyed in a riot caused by Zam Wesell. Needing a replacement, he broke into the prison's hangar of six prototype [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft/Legends|''Firespray''-class starships]] in one of the hangars of the asteroid prison. Stealing one and demolishing the other five, he christened it ''"Slave I"'', which he used up until his death. The ship would later go into the hands of his son, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].<ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" />

==Behind the scenes==
Jango Fett was portrayed by [[Temuera Morrison]] and stunt double [[Scott McLean]] in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] and voiced by Morrison in the video games ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''.<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /><ref name="Star Wars: Bounty Hunter" /><ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> [[Bob Marshall]] portrayed Fett in a commercial but the voice was provided by an unknown actor ILM filmed for ''Star Wars: Bounty Hunter''.<ref name="D1">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/bountyhunter_ad.html|text=''Star Wars'' Bounty Hunter Commercial}}</ref> [[Jeff Bennett]] provided Fett's voice in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter]]''.

"www.ambufett.com" was a domain name purchased by [[Lucasfilm]] before the release of ''Attack of the Clones''.<ref name="ESGH">{{Blog|arfmaul|21|Domain names: Ambu Fett, and.... Stiffy Borborygmus???}}</ref> It is possible that Ambu Fett may have been considered as the original name of Fett, or another [[Clan Fett|Fett family]] member, or perhaps another clone. Another name proposed for the character was J'mee Fett.<ref name="db" />

In the "Creating Mandalore" featurette on [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|''The Clone Wars'': Season Two]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|DVD set]], series director [[Dave Filoni]] explained that, according to [[George Lucas]], the Fetts were not Mandalorians.<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]]</ref>

There is a discrepancy in the time during which Fett spends with [[Sheeka Tull]]; in two locations in ''[[The Cestus Deception]]'' it is specifically said they met in [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]]; however, Sheeka also says that they met two years after the [[Battle of Galidraan|destruction of the Mandalorians]], which took place in [[34 BBY/Legends|34 BBY]].<ref name="The Cestus Deception" /> [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']] retconned this difference by establishing that the Battle of Galidraan took place ten years earlier, in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]].<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

Jango also is a secret skateboarder in the video game [[Wikipedia:Tony Hawk_Pro Skater 4|''Tony Hawk: Pro Skater 4'']]. He can be bought for $9000. He also can fire his blaster whilst grinding and launch a grappling hook in mid-air.

===Non-canonical biographical information===
{{Noncanonstart|legends=1}}
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Fett followed up on an advertisement to find a template for a clone army disguised as an advertisement to become a Mandalorian. Fett participated in a "last man standing" shootout known as "[[Fett Club (comic story)|Fett Club]]," which he won with the aid of [[Kannen Doom]]. After that, a man named Tyranus then hired him to be the template for a clone army at his price and he was told to report to Kamino.<ref name="Fett Club">{{Tales|24|Fett Club (comic story)}}</ref>
{{Noncanonend}}
